'''David Roy Davies''' (12 August 1928 – 14 July 2013) was a [[Welsh people|Welsh]] [[cricket]]er.  Davies was a right-handed [[batsman (cricket)|batsman]].  He was born at [[Llanelli]], [[Carmarthenshire]].  He was educated in his later early years at [[Cardiff University]].

Davies made a single [[first-class cricket|first-class]] appearance for [[Glamorgan County Cricket Club|Glamorgan]] in 1950 against [[Somerset County Cricket Club|Somerset]].<ref>[https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/4/4386/First-Class_Matches.html First-Class Matches played by Roy Davies]</ref>  In the match, he scored 7 runs in his only first-class innings.<ref>[https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/4/4386/f_Batting_by_Team.html First-class Batting and Fielding For Each Team by Roy Davies]</ref>

Davies was an [[Industrial chemistry|industrial chemist]] and fuel technologist who later worked for [[Unilever]]. Davies also played [[Squash (sport)|squash]], a sport he represented Wales in.

==Family==
Davies had an older brother, [[Haydn Davies (cricketer)|Haydn]], who played first-class cricket for Glamorgan and the [[Marylebone Cricket Club]].  Both of their parents were killed during the [[Second World War]], after which Haydn adopted Roy and became his legal father.<ref>[https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Articles/1/1204.html Brief profile of Roy Davies]</ref>  His nephew [[Andrew Davies (cricketer, born 1962)|Andrew Davies]] played first-class cricket for [[Cambridge University Cricket Club|Cambridge University]] and [[List-A cricket]] for the [[British Universities cricket team|Combined Universities]].
